V-M-SERVICE-TELEMETRY.Scenario: A GT7 UDP packet is received, decrypted with Salsa20 and mapped to TelemetryData with speed, RPM, tyre, fuel and gear values matching the game state.
A malformed or truncated packet is rejected without killing the listener, and the next valid packet still updates the state.

V-M-SERVICE-UDP.Scenario: The listener binds the telemetry port, reports the local address it will receive on, and stops cleanly on dispose.
A port already in use surfaces as a socket error instead of a silent no-op.

V-M-MODEL-TELEMETRY.Scenario: Raw decoded bytes map to the documented field set, including tyre temperatures and the throttle/brake pair.
A short packet leaves the optional fields null rather than producing wrong values.

V-M-MODEL-TRACK-TRACE.Scenario: A recorded trace keeps packet order and closes the path when the lap restarts.

V-M-WIDGET-TELEMETRY.Command: flutter test test/telemetry_display_layout_test.dart test/motion_panel_layout_test.dart test/car_model_3d_test.dart test/surface_codes_test.dart
V-M-WIDGET-TELEMETRY.Scenario: Telemetry and motion layouts build at phone and desktop widths without overflow.
Surface code labels match the game's grip codes.
A missing or unknown surface code renders the neutral label instead of throwing.

V-M-BLOC-THROTTLE-BRAKE.Scenario: Clutch and throttle/brake samples are windowed in packet order.

V-M-SERVICE-DG-EDGE.Scenario: Both frozen fixtures (race list, player profile) parse into the expected counts and first item.
A non-200 response surfaces as an error state instead of an empty list.
A live page redesign parses to zero cards: covered by the network-tagged diagnostic `flutter test --tags network --run-skipped test/live_markup_guard_test.dart`.

V-M-SERVICE-GTSH-RANK.Scenario: Ranking cards parse with leader and slipstream fields populated.
The live site renaming its card class is caught by the network-tagged diagnostic `flutter test --tags network --run-skipped test/live_markup_guard_test.dart`.

V-M-REPO-SPORT.Scenario: Races pair on the game's board id and unpaired GTSh cards still appear in the merged list.
The merged list orders upcoming before active before past, keeping upstream order inside a group.
When one source fails the other half is still published, and the aggregate error appears only when both are empty.

V-M-MODEL-DAILY.Scenario: DailyRace.fromPair fills the unified fields from whichever source provides them and keeps the other side nullable.
A race without a track name is dropped rather than rendered as a blank card.

V-M-WIDGET-DAILY.Scenario: The daily races screen renders the expected race sections and hides past races when asked to.

V-M-SERVICE-GT7INFO.Scenario: Used and legendary lists parse from the site's payload with prices and stock state.
A site change yields an empty list plus an error state, never a silent empty success.

V-M-SERVICE-GTDB.Scenario: The GraphQL query returns cars with artwork identifiers that the card can resolve.
A missing artwork id falls back to the GT7 thumbnail instead of a broken image.

V-M-REPO-CAR.Scenario: The bundled car catalogue loads and answers id to name and photo lookups.
Merged gt7info and GTDB rows split into the used and legendary lists without duplicates.
One source failing still publishes the other source's cars.

V-M-MODEL-CAR.Scenario: Car type codes map to their expected labels and categories.
An unknown code yields null rather than a plausible-looking wrong value.

V-M-WIDGET-CAR-DEALER.Scenario: Used and legendary screens render their grids at phone and desktop widths and open the price history on tap.

The vertical keeps a single definition of each shared fragment: the stock badge and the error panel live once and both screens adopt them, so a change to their padding, radius or copy cannot drift between the used and legendary cards.

A colour literal in this vertical stays inside 0..255: the used-card decoration resolves to alpha 24/255, and an out-of-range argument such as the historical withAlpha(280) counts as a defect even though the SDK masks it silently with & 0xff.
A missing car image renders the placeholder instead of collapsing the card.

V-M-MODEL-GT-AUTO.Scenario: The GT Auto catalogue exposes the counters used by the screen.

V-M-WIDGET-GT-AUTO.Scenario: The GT Auto screen lists counters and opens a counter view with its multiplier.
Selecting a counter that has no data keeps the previous selection instead of rendering an empty view.

V-M-SERVICE-GT7-AUTH.Scenario: Secret fields are masked in every trace line.
A token that reaches a log line is redacted, never printed verbatim.
Concurrent refresh calls share one in-flight token exchange.

V-M-SERVICE-GT7-API.Scenario: A successful call returns the decoded body and clears the error state.
A 401 triggers exactly one token refresh and one retry, then reports the error and invalidates the token.

V-M-SERVICE-NETWORK-SCANNER.Scenario: The scanner reports hosts that answer on the Remote Play port with a PlayStation-like hostname.
A subnet that cannot be determined returns an empty result plus a logged reason, not an exception.

V-M-REPO-GT7-AUTH.Scenario: A stored token restores a signed-in profile without a new login.
An expired token clears the session and reports signed-out rather than looping on refresh.

V-M-REPO-TRACK.Scenario: The course catalogue loads and answers a track name for a known lap length.

V-M-PAGE-LOGIN.Scenario: The WebView completes the PSN consent flow, the session is exchanged for a token and the page pops true.
A cancelled or failed login pops false and leaves no partial session.

V-M-PAGE-WISHLIST.Scenario: The wishlist screen renders the cars the player saved and survives an empty list.

V-M-SHELL-HOME.Scenario: The home hub composes the telemetry panel, the daily races section and the service tile grid at phone and desktop widths.
A section whose repository is still loading does not block the rest of the hub.

V-M-SHELL-TABS.Scenario: The tab shell switches between home, wishlist, profile and telemetry while keeping each tab's state.

V-M-NAVBAR.Scenario: The navbar marks the active tab and switches it through TabsRouter.
When no TabsRouter is available the navbar falls back to popping back to the home route instead of throwing.

V-M-DI-APPSCOPE.Scenario: Every provider in the scope resolves and depends only on providers registered above it.
Removing a provider surfaces as a ProviderNotFoundError in the widget that consumes it, not as a null service.

V-M-ROUTER.Scenario: Every route in app_router.dart resolves and the generated app_router.gr.dart matches the declarations.
A missing @RoutePage() shows up as a failed generation step rather than a runtime route miss.

V-M-THEME.Scenario: gt7Theme() builds a dark ColorScheme with the full text theme and the graph ThemeExtension registered.
A widget asking for a ColorScheme slot that the theme does not define falls back to the surface colour instead of throwing.

V-M-SOUND.Scenario: With sound switched on, each effect the interface asks for is played exactly once.
With sound switched off the service calls the player zero times: silence is the expected outcome here, not a failure.
A press, a route push and a route pop each make their own sound, and the app's first route is excluded because it is not a navigation the user made.
A repeat of the same effect inside the 40 ms window is dropped, so a fast tapper cannot machine-gun clicks.
With music switched on, a track starts when the service loads and the next one follows when the current one finishes, wrapping back to the first at the end of the rotation.
With music switched off the player is never asked to start: silence is the expected outcome, not a failure, and the same holds for the track-completion path.
The music pauses when the app leaves the foreground and returns only while the channel is enabled, so a backgrounded companion is silent.

V-M-FEATURE-PROFILE.Scenario: Profile loading moves through loading to a populated state, and stats parse from the enveloped API shape.
A failed profile fetch ends in an error state instead of an empty success.
